notes: DOCUMENTED TARGET - NOT RECORDABLE (agent_supports: no). This spec states the arc the row asserts so a future re-assessment has something concrete to compare against; it is NOT expected to pass on hermes as it stands, and it is deliberately not weakened to match what hermes can do. THE ROW: two DISTINCT waiting episodes in one session - one raised by a MUTATING tool, one raised by a READ-ONLY tool - with the arc ready -> working -> waiting -> working -> waiting -> working -> ready and a final ready that survives a >=10s trailing idle. AGENT LAYER (the half that fails): hermes 0.19.0 opens a human permission dialog on exactly two default surfaces, both mutating - the `terminal` shell tool (tools/approval.py:3180 check_all_command_guards, whose only non-test importer is tools/terminal_tool.py:256) and `execute_code` (check_execute_code_guard, :3637) - plus an opt-in memory/skills WRITE gate (tools/write_approval.py, default false). Every read-only tool in the roster was checked at its own implementing module and none references the approval system: read_file and search_files (tools/file_tools.py - two comments, zero calls), session_search, web_search, web_extract, browser_snapshot, read_terminal. hermes' read-side guards are REFUSALS handed to the model (file_tools.py:595 'Refusing to write to sensitive system path'; _search_result_read_block_error drops blocked paths out of a search result), never a modal a user answers - structurally the opposite of antigravity's ask_permission tool call. The only route to a read-tool dialog is an operator-installed pre_tool_call plugin rule calling tools/approval.py:2947 request_tool_approval, which would record a fabricated gate. WHAT THE PHASES BELOW DO NOT EXPRESS: the phase schema carries no tool-name field, so nothing here can bind gate1 and gate2 to two DIFFERENT tools. That binding is the whole row. If this cell is ever unfrozen, the verify must assert it out of band - otherwise a recipe driving two `terminal` calls (one read-only command like `cat`, one mutating like `rm`) makes every phase below green while testing nothing about tool class, because both episodes are the same shell tool and both reach exactly the allowlist-shaped integration #1861 describes. The phase ORDER (mutating first) is arbitrary and is NOT part of the row's claim. TRANSPORT LAYER (the second, independent blocker): hermes writes no transcript files - the daemon reads the shared $HERMES_HOME/state.db (ProcessOwnedStore) and, since this branch, three installed shell hooks (pre_approval_request / post_approval_response / on_session_end). A plugin-raised read-tool gate would reach NEITHER: the store has no approval table and the assistant tool_calls row is flushed before dispatch, and hermes' _fire_approval_hook has only four call sites (approval.py:154, :162, :3099, :3167, :3576, :3592) - none of them in _run_approval_gate (2644-2862), the shared gate request_tool_approval returns through. ANCHORING follows this column's ProcessOwnedStore shape: the sessions row is INSERTed only on the first user message, so session_birth is anchored to recording start and left UNPINNED (the ready birth in a recording is the transient proc-<PID> pre-session), and every later phase chains through same_session_as: turn_start. NO observations block: of verify hard-asserts only against the newest recording's replay-golden summary (internal/validate/observations.go:141-160), hermes' Parser sets only ev.ModelName (parser.go:78), and the store-derived token lift is gated to antigravity (cmd/replay/metrics.go:59) - so tokens_nonzero and cost_nonzero could never pass here, and model would be a doc-guess on a cell that is never recorded.

text: A hermes session appears in ready shortly after launch (expected to be the transient proc-<PID> pre-session - the store row does not exist until the first user message)
A PID is bound to the session (hermes is a Python console script, matched on the full command line)
The prompt that needs both a mutating and a read-only tool call drives the store-backed session ready -> working
The first permission dialog opens and the session goes working -> waiting while the modal is on screen. On hermes this is the MUTATING half (a gated `terminal` command) - the half 2.19 already covers
The user answers the first dialog and the session resumes waiting -> working

THE PHASE THIS ROW EXISTS FOR. A second, DISTINCT permission dialog - raised by a tool that only READS (a file read, a code search, a directory listing, a web fetch) - produces its own waiting episode. It is not skipped and it is not merged into gate1's episode. hermes has no such tool gate, which is why this cell is frozen
The user answers the second dialog and the session resumes waiting -> working
The turn finishes back to ready - full arc ready -> working -> waiting -> working -> waiting -> working -> ready
The session is still ready after a >=10s trailing idle: it does not remain waiting after the last dialog closes, and no late post-tool signal bounces it back
